question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/f25b8fea7403579d1ee40cc00b9447e3362dc28c2e9d41f762f51df5e11daaf8.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>2.31).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/a3e01ca4fd737cea9afe95374a17c0428f83a6717d98a7557222a856aa2d0c02.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<-2.31).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/ce206061194e357b9cd75f9b260e4035a8600726a17cc0ee04ab39219bd45e94.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>2.31)=P(Z<-2.31)=Φ(-2.31)=0.0104.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval Using the Complement
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/597125714057269b7adf9c0a2a9bbdde9631cf37bc80518281ab4444c3189717.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<-0.73).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/3e4fb2143266d45a620bf39a978ba8ac4f0ed2585942f79dc90435a4896f9a0d.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>0.73).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/6bb24449a20276b9d190e2b31926bb6e0d52f22536431e27c05db00b92886ffc.png)

Note that the two shaded areas above have the same area. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-0.73) & =P(Z>0.73) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.73) \\  & =1-Φ(0.73) \\  & =1-0.7673 \\  & =0.2327.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on a Bounded Interval
question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.18<Z<0.18).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/061aec33cb30172ec64c89841fc70cb2e5bec9b89f92ef0427ff9673bfa99219.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.18<Z<0.18) & =P(Z<0.18)-P(Z\le -0.18) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.18)-P(Z\le -0.18) \\  & =Φ(0.18)-Φ(-0.18)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-0.18)=0.4286,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(0.18).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.18) & =P(Z\le 0.18) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.18) \\  & =1-P(Z<-0.18) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.18) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.18) \\  & =1-0.4286 \\  & =0.5714\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.18<Z<0.18) & =Φ(0.18)-Φ(-0.18) \\  & =0.5714-0.4286 \\  & =0.1428.\end{aligned}
$$
